title: Issue citation list, schema version 2
description: One file per issue, data/citations/{serial}.json, listing every source that issue cites -- the input the source registry (data/sources/registry.json) and the evidence manifests (data/evidence/) are built from. Order matters: it is the order REF numbers are assigned in the evidence manifest, so append new citations rather than reordering. v2 adds type_basis (classification spec §21 amendment): 'type' is author-supplied, a change from the pipeline auto-assigning it from domain/publisher name, and type_basis is where the author records what the publisher's own self-description actually said, so the judgment call is checkable. type_basis is optional rather than required, on purpose -- every citation recorded under v1 (schema version 1) has no such field, and backfilling one now would be inventing a self-description nobody actually read at the time. Required for anything cited going forward; absent, not fabricated, on what's already on file.

canonical_name.description: Reuse the exact string already in the registry for this domain where one exists, so this citation folds into the same registry entry instead of minting a duplicate.

type.description: Classification spec §3. Author-supplied: the citing author reads the publisher's self-description and assigns the type, per classification spec §21's amendment. This makes the source-record denominators in §12 author-influenced rather than mechanical, and that is disclosed via type_basis rather than folded into housekeeping.

type_basis.description: The publisher's self-description, verbatim, in the citing author's own words -- what the site says about itself, not a judgment about whether that's accurate. Optional: absent on anything cited before this field existed (schema v1), required going forward.

origin.description: Two-letter country code. Absent where not established with confidence; never guessed.
